forecasts.question: Will Iran resume negotiations with the US before EOD 2026-06-16?

Iran's June 1 suspension of negotiations remained in force without formal rescission before that date. The sixth round planned for June 15 was cancelled following Israeli strikes on June 13. Al Jazeera's June 16 reporting stated nuclear talks would 'begin after framework deal signing,' referring forward to the June 19 ceremony — a future-tense reference, not a backward rescission of the June 1 suspension. The electronic relay of MOU text circa June 14-15 constituted a written-message procedure, not a convened session under the resolution criteria. Ambiguity rule applied: AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

A held mediated session counts; mere rhetorical assertion that 'talks continue' or relay of written messages does NOT count.

forecasts.question: Will the US-Iran 60-day MOU structured negotiations produce a signed nuclear framework agreement (covering HEU limits and permanent Hormuz status) before EOD 2026-08-18?
forecasts.delta_reason: New forecast. The Islamabad MOU is a 14-point framework without specified HEU limits, verification protocols, IAEA access arrangements, sanctions relief schedules, or permanent Hormuz governance terms. Resolving all elements within 60 days requires both sides to accept constraints that domestic constituencies oppose: Iran's IRGC-aligned hardliners reject HEU limits (Kayhan, Fars confirmed); US congressional and Israeli pressure demands intrusive verification. Historical precedent (JCPOA: 20 months) suggests the 60-day timeline is highly compressed. Base case: talks proceed but framework remains partial or deadline extends. A complete signed agreement covering both HEU and permanent Hormuz terms within the window is a tail-positive outcome. 0.20 reflects the structural constraint argument per DA opposing narrative accepted by Judge.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: A signed document — confirmed by TIER1 sources and acknowledged by both the US and Iranian governments — must specify: (1) explicit limits on Iranian high-enriched uranium (HEU) production or stockpile levels; AND (2) a permanent or long-term governance framework for Hormuz transit rights. Both elements must be present in the signed text. A renewal or extension of the MOU ceasefire without these specifics does not qualify.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: TIER1 reporting citing the full text or official government summaries of the agreement. State media claims without independent TIER1 corroboration are insufficient.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If a document is signed but one element (HEU limits OR Hormuz governance) is described as 'to be negotiated' or 'in principle,' resolve AMBIGUOUS-AS-NO. An extension of the MOU ceasefire without the required specifics resolves NO.
